items.title: Daily nicotine vaping in young never-smokers linked to impaired vascular function and lower fitness (JAMA Cardiology)
items.summary: In a small UK cross-sectional study of 58 healthy young adults, daily nicotine vape users had lower endothelial function and peak VO2 than never-users; cigarette smokers also had lower endothelial function (JAMA Cardiology, Oct 21, 2026).
bullets: Design: single-centre cross-sectional study from Manchester Metropolitan University of 58 healthy young adults (mean age 26): 17 exclusive daily nicotine vape users, 19 cigarette smokers and 22 never-users; smoking status was self-reported and verified.

Vascular function: mean FMD was 5.5% in vapers and 4.4% in smokers vs 8.3% in never-users; carotid artery reactivity was 0.6% and -1.4% vs 4.7%. Per the university, vapers did not differ significantly from light smokers.

Fitness: peak VO2 was lower in vapers than in never-users but not significantly lower in smokers; minute ventilation and cardiac output on maximal exercise testing were lower in both nicotine groups. Lung function and physical activity did not differ.
Per the university release, the findings held in vapers who had never been regular smokers; the authors say vaping may help smokers who switch completely, but never-smokers should not vape.
Limits: small, locally recruited volunteers and cross-sectional design, so it cannot show cause and effect; longitudinal studies are needed to see if these changes lead to cardiovascular disease.
items.source: Boidin M, et al. JAMA Cardiology, Oct 21, 2026. doi:10.1001/jamacardio.2026.4626
